subject: Science
stem: Among all the planets in our solar system, this planet is the largest by both size and mass, and is famous for its Great Red Spot (a giant, centuries-old storm). It is:
explanation: Jupiter is the solar system's largest planet by far — Saturn is second-largest and best known for its prominent ring system, while Uranus and Neptune are the smaller, more distant ice giants.

subject: Science
stem: A small, icy celestial body that develops a glowing tail of gas and dust as it approaches the Sun (its orbit visible only periodically from Earth, as with Halley's Comet), is called a:
explanation: Comets are icy bodies that develop a visible tail from solar heating as they near the Sun — distinct from asteroids (rocky bodies, mostly in the belt between Mars and Jupiter, without a tail) or meteors (streaks of light from debris burning in Earth's atmosphere).

subject: Science
stem: Since Earth actually takes about 365.25 days (not exactly 365) to revolve around the Sun, an extra day (29 February) is added to the calendar once every four years to keep it aligned with the seasons. This extra day makes that year a:
explanation: A leap year (366 days, with an added 29 February) compensates for the quarter-day discrepancy between Earth's actual orbital period (~365.25 days) and the standard 365-day calendar year, keeping the calendar synced with Earth's revolution.

subject: Science
stem: The changing shapes of the Moon we see over about a month — from a thin crescent to a full circle and back — occur because:

options.option_text: We see different portions of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth
The Moon's own shape physically changes over the month
The Moon moves closer to and farther from the Sun each month
Clouds on Earth block different parts of the Moon

explanation: The Moon's phases result from the changing angle at which we view its permanently sunlit half as it orbits Earth — the Moon itself does not change shape or move toward/away from the Sun on a monthly cycle; only our viewing angle of its illuminated portion changes.
